result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.

result.rule: When the description states that a participant performs a distinct action to initiate the process: Model a start event for the process trigger, followed by a task for the initiating action; do not use the start event to represent the action itself.

When the description states that the process begins when an incoming communication or request occurs, without describing separate work to receive it: Represent that occurrence with a suitable start event; model a separate receipt activity only when the description states that receiving it is work to be performed.

When the description states that information is recorded in a system before a subsequent handling action: Model the recording as a distinct activity and connect it in sequence before that handling action.

When the description presents activities or events in a chronological sequence, including how the process begins: Connect the corresponding BPMN elements with sequence flows in the stated order, including a flow from the start event to the first activity and flows between successive activities.
